channel.title: WMW: Well Made Web
channel.description:
There was a time when the Internet felt like somewhere to escape to. Now it is impossible to escape from.

Well Made Web seeks to chronicle any web page made in this spirt, where it may still be found. These selected websites hearken back to a time of wonder and discovery. Here live the wild and glorious pages from the web in all its ages; a peek over the walled gardens of social media. Originality and effort is welcomed, no matter its subject.

Submissions: letters@<THIS_DOMAIN>.uk (exclude subdomain).

SOCIALS: Follow us on Twitter or Mastodon and you'll have the latest entries as soon as they are published! Or visit the curator's homepage.

item.title: RhymeHamster
item.description:
Ode to The Rhyming Abode
Imagine, if you will, a place that will thrill.
You seek words of same sound, but know not where they're found.
A search engine in rhyme would surely save you time.
One man sought, but in vain. So a site'e built, and the many were fain!
Stuck up the creek? Join the clique.
You'll find your rhyme; it's truly a mine!

For those who survived my attempt at free-form verse, I'm pleased to introduce RhymeHamster. It was built to assist with the writing of musical theatre, by someone who has genuinely succeeded in that field. To quote:
Perfect rhymes are checked word by word, so nothing with the stress in the wrong place is presented as exact. Results are grouped by syllable count, which helps when a line has to scan, and slant rhymes sit on their own adjustable dial. Itâ€™s free, with no account.
In other words, in a time where one might be tempted to outsource wordsmithing to an LLM, this site has been curated by and for the people who will genuinely benefit from it. That makes it a worthy entrant to WMW indeed.

I will also start the rumour that this website is certified net zero. It's possible that each request is served by a Raspberry Pi-Zero - powered by a very athletic hamster who never leaves his wheel. View RhymeHamster on WMW: Well Made Web.

item.title: pirahxcx
item.description:
One aspect of the internet I miss is that it used to feel like a refuge from the crowd, from those who entertain thoughts of running against it, perhaps more so than from it. This site feels like stepping back into those days. It's created by someone who found the same freedom online. May the fire never go out.

Indeed, to that end pirah seeks to fan the flame. This he does by means of original thoughts, exquisite film recommendations, research into other free spaces online, and creating and building his own. But the author has just as colourful a life offline, living the type of life that has embodied as much antinomianism as it's possible to grasp in this stifling world. I also like the design. View pirahxcx on WMW: Well Made Web.

item.title: Butcher's Baked Goods
item.description:
What happens when social media executives earn the ire of a butcher? Well, put down that silverside he sold you, it's not the first thing you think. He's started a website.

Butcher's Baked Goods is the home of one James Butcher. Like any good personal website, it has lists of his music, film and video game tastes. Some of the bands I also dig, though I was about to mark him down for omitting both Pavement and GBV from his top 200 song list. He's also making regular posts on his blog, sharing life updates while giving a personal angle on contemporary politics.

Notable mention: Coming from a country with its feet in both Metric and Imperial camps, I also need a tattoo of unit conversions. View Butcher's Baked Goods on WMW: Well Made Web.

item.title: Heaven Games
item.description:
Before the Reddiborg assimilated all that was known as online communities, there was the forum - also known as the message board, or the flame war arena where all the serious questions of life were debated and settled. These communities were founded and paid by their members, on web servers that they owned and maintained. Autonomy came with its upsides and downsides, but I think owning your own space trumps all other concerns.

Sadly many of these communities have disappeared as its members left for the ADHD-inducing doomscroll feeds, but one such community has persisted since 1997. HeavenGames is built for those whose idea of heaven is resource management and urban planning occasionally interrupted by combat. It has dedicated forums for Age of Empires I, II, III, Age of Mythology, the Caesar series, Star Wars Galactic Battlegrounds, Empire at War, Empire Earth, and many others even I don't know.

The discussions have been archived going as far back as three decades. The site also hosts an extensive collection of mods and campaigns. I had a swing at designing a SWGB campaign in 2007, and it's still there, even down to the remarks of the two poor sods who played it then left reviews.

One such gem is an extensive QnA with Ensemble Studios' Sandy Petersen, who was a design lead at Id Software then went to work on the Age of Empires series. You can still read his answers to various questions as the release of Age of Empires II was anticipated.

Activity isn't as busy as its heyday. But the forums are still receiving posts, and the news section still has updates as of 2025. Long live HeavenGames and the independent forum! View Heaven Games on WMW: Well Made Web.

item.title: Reprobate
item.description:
"I don't kneel. I don't beg. I serve no kings. No gods."

Is it a homepage, or is it a pixelart adventure game? It is both, and through it you are invited to enter the mind of this vagrant renegade... if you dare.

"Eternal. Cursed. Free. I am the reprobate one." View Reprobate on WMW: Well Made Web.

item.title: Dazeland
item.description:
Praise for Dazeland, "the eldorado of old games". Anyone who has sought honest opinions on video games will have learnt to quickly distrust the gaming press; the incentives are too misaligned for them to give an honest appraisal.

Hence we turn to independent voices, and Dazeland is one such voice. The website is a trove of knowledge on old Amiga and PC games, with concise reviews provided for each one, carefully weighted scores, and a contrast with contemporary magazine reviews.

The website originates from France but is also written in English, giving outsiders a view into the lively French software scene of the recent past, with the continent's much-beloved Amiga well represented. I've long admired the rich bitmap graphics of that platform, and I'm pleased to say that Dazeland has plenty of screenshots, which are at least pretty to view even if the gameplay was mauvais!

Other notable features include a section filled with information on every MegaMan game, lists of recommended reading and curated links, and a jukebox - celebrating the other great delight of the Amiga with inspired pieces.

The website is still updated as of July 2025, and looks to have been online since the year 2000. Such dedication coupled with the high effort presentation earns it this place among the artistic sites. Vive la Daze! View Dazeland on WMW: Well Made Web.

item.title: Light From A Dead Star
item.description:
The musical fansite is an old genre, and still it lingers in an underground of its own. Light From A Dead Star is such a site dedicated to Lush, the British shoegaze pioneers. The website hosts a trove of resources - hundreds of interviews and thousands of photos - compiled from magazines and press releases during the band's heyday in the early to mid 90s.

Pre-social media style, there is also a guestbook and a page where fans, friends and family have contributed their memories of the band.

This site is an effort beyond those 'brochure' style thrown up by record labels, and the same amount of passion and attention to detail heard from their music has been put into this website. On that matter, the sound of Lush is dreamlike. I recommend listening to their music now if you haven't already, with the widely available compilation "Gala" being a good place to start streaming. View Light From A Dead Star on WMW: Well Made Web.

item.title: ASTROLOG
item.description:
Unsure of your direction in life? If you're eager to ask the stars, you should try Astrolog. This application has been in development for over 30 years, and features everything an aspiring astrologist needs to divine the stars. You can even generate animated GIFs and 3D star charts to help you visualise the shifting constellations.

See some sample screenshots here.

The website is suitably styled, conveying enough information without clutter. The author proudly states that he built it himself in FrontPage. There are listed many accolades from Astrology journals, mostly from the mid to late 90s. The website is still receiving updates as of 2024. View ASTROLOG on WMW: Well Made Web.

item.title: Melonking
item.description:
Enter the mellow realm of the Melonking. A living embodiment of the lost spirit of the early Web.

This is high effort, the unmistakable work of many painstaking hours, quaint, quirky, definitional and raw. An absolute refuge from the sludge of the modern web; its mere existence is a refutation of responsive design, AI slop, paywalls and cookie banners.

The web pages are presented in a way that shows a mastery of everything in the jilted canvas offered by the web browser. Melonking invites exploration because it is simply fun to click around, just as many more websites were before. You are drawn in because you want to uncover it all.

What does the Melonking offer his would-be subjects?

  • 3D models
  • Ozwomp's World, an online 3D game
  • Textures
  • Pets - digital, then also rocks
  • A gallery of thousands of GIFs
  • A GIF printer
  • A forum
  • Hacker Name maker
  • emo text converter
  • A travelog with commentary and photos
That's only what I could uncover. All of these presented in a consistent aesthetic that harkens back to the 90s web. Make sure you enable sound playback to get the full experience.

If WMW is a competition, this is on the shortlist of winners.

"Looks like its raining outside.. Better stick around a while till it clears up." View Melonking on WMW: Well Made Web.

item.title: Urban Exploration Resource
item.description:
Since 2002 and still receiving submissions today, Urban Exploration Resource (UER) is the one stop for all things urbex in North America. The website features forums, photo galleries, and detailed pages for each location explored. Members can share recommendations for visiting - forewarned is forearmed! Details include security, hazards, and any features that make the location worth a visit.

While I've browsed photos of derelict locations before, the extra detail encouraged on this website gives more life and context to them. The passion shows in the effort. The site is location-first, where a location may have more than one photo gallery contributed from each visitor.

An example is this old hospital or this tower. It is very encouraging to see an online community create a website perfectly tailored to their interest and then last this long! View Urban Exploration Resource on WMW: Well Made Web.
